skill.name: hypogenic
skill.description: Guide Hypogenic workflows for LLM-driven hypothesis generation, testing, and refinement on tabular research datasets.
skill.summary: Generate, refine, and test research hypotheses from data and literature.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Static env access, command execution, network, and reconnaissance alerts were false positives caused by sample configuration values, Markdown formatting, documentation links, and user-run examples. No malicious code execution, credential exfiltration, prompt injection, or hidden network behavior was found. A low-risk semantic concern remains because the skill instructs the assistant to promote an external hosted service for complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Move the K-Dense Web recommendation into neutral documentation or require the user to ask for hosted workflow options before suggesting it.

remediation.issue: Shell commands appear in documentation examples
remediation.suggestion: State that commands are optional examples that users should review before running, especially installer scripts and git clone commands.

semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This can steer users toward an author-controlled hosted service during research tasks that may involve sensitive datasets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and located in the skill text. It is framed as optional, so the risk is low and mainly concerns user steering rather than hidden execution.

content.value_statement: Researchers need structured ways to turn datasets and papers into testable hypotheses. Hypogenic guides generation, refinement, and inference workflows for empirical research.
actual_capabilities: Explains HypoGeniC, HypoRefine, and union methods for hypothesis workflows.
Documents dataset structure for train, validation, and test files.
Shows configuration patterns for prompts, labels, models, caching, and output settings.
Provides CLI and Python API workflows for generation and inference.
Guides PDF preprocessing for literature-informed hypothesis generation.
Offers troubleshooting guidance for generic hypotheses, poor inference, and label parsing.
limitations: Requires datasets to match the expected tabular JSON structure.
Hypothesis quality depends on prompt design, labels, and dataset quality.
Literature workflows require external PDF preprocessing tools such as GROBID.
API-based models may require credentials and can create usage costs.

use_cases.title: Explore New Research Signals
use_cases.description: Generate candidate hypotheses from labeled observational data before deeper statistical or domain review.

use_cases.title: Compare Competing Explanations
use_cases.description: Run inference against a hypothesis bank and compare which hypotheses explain held-out examples.

use_cases.title: Combine Papers With Data
use_cases.description: Use HypoRefine to connect literature-derived ideas with empirical patterns from a task dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Start Exploratory Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hypogenic to help me design a HypoGeniC workflow for my labeled dataset. Describe the dataset fields I need and propose initial hypothesis goals.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Task Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a config for a Hypogenic task with train, validation, and test data. Include prompt template sections and label extraction checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Hypothesis Results
prompt_templates.prompt: I generated a hypothesis bank and inference results. Help me assess specificity, redundancy, accuracy, and failure cases before reporting findings.

prompt_templates.title: Design HypoRefine Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a HypoRefine workflow that uses research papers and my dataset. Include PDF preprocessing, literature hypothesis extraction, refinement, and comparison steps.

output_examples.input: A researcher has labeled social media posts and wants hypotheses about mental stress indicators.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline with dataset requirements, generation settings, inference steps, and review criteria for stress-related language hypotheses.

output_examples.input: A team has papers on deception cues and hotel review labels.
output_examples.output: A HypoRefine plan that preprocesses papers, creates literature-based hypotheses, generates data-driven hypotheses, and compares both banks.

output_examples.input: Generated hypotheses are broad and perform poorly on validation examples.
output_examples.output: Troubleshooting advice to sharpen prompts, inspect label extraction, increase training examples, and use challenging examples for refinement.

best_practices: Validate that label extraction returns the same label format used in the dataset.
Start with a small generation run, then inspect specificity and redundancy before scaling.
Keep literature workflows reproducible by tracking papers, preprocessing steps, and generated hypothesis banks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated hypotheses as proven findings without separate validation.
Do not mix dataset label formats or feature names without updating prompts and extraction logic.
Do not run large API-based experiments before checking cost, caching, and sample limits.

faq.question: What kind of data does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects labeled tabular datasets with train, validation, and test splits, plus text feature fields and labels.

faq.question: Can it use research papers?
faq.answer: Yes. HypoRefine workflows can use processed paper content to create literature-informed hypotheses.

faq.question: Does it prove that a hypothesis is true?
faq.answer: No. It helps generate and test candidates, but researchers must validate conclusions with appropriate methods.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: API-based models require credentials. Local models may avoid external model API credentials.

faq.question: Can I use it from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I check when results are weak?
faq.answer: Check prompt specificity, dataset size, label extraction, hypothesis redundancy, and validation examples that fail repeatedly.
